subject: Setting xlim() with geom_area *increases* the range of the y axis (sometimes significantly)

messages.author: d19b7d669a70af7c
messages.subject: Setting xlim() with geom_area *increases* the range of the y axis (sometimes significantly)
parts:
ggplot2 is super nice. I'm hoping the following is simply me being
confused.

Appending xlim() to a geom_area plot sometimes *increases* the range
shown on the *y* axis. Can that be right? Example: The following
produces the area plot I would expect: The y scale on the chart ranges
from 0 to 3.:

some_data <- data.frame(x = c(1,2,3,4,5), y = c(2,3,2,3,2))
qplot(data = some_data, x = x, y = y, geom = "area")

But now, the following results in a y scale ranging from 0 to 5 (even
though, clearly, the maximum y can be no greater than in the previous
example):

last_plot() + xlim(c(1,3))

Indeed, last_plot() + xlim(c(2,3)) results in a y-axis that ranges
from 0 to 7! What am I missing here? (The same behaviour is observed
if I write out the plot in full, rather than using last_plot() and
also if I use scale_x_continuous() rather than xlim()). However, using
coord_cartesian(xlim = c(2,3)) produces the plot I would expect --
with the y scale ranging from 0 to 3 as in the original plot.

I wouldn't mind, but it's extremely convenient to have an automatic y
scale in my actual application; unfortunately, the y scale chosen
automatically is so large that the graph is unreadably tiny; using
coord_cartesian() is a pain because I have an awful lot of points and
the chart takes forever to draw.

Any help (or enlightenment) greatly appreciated.

James


[R version 2.11.1 and ggplot 0.8.8 on OS X 10.6.4]

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Setting xlim() with geom_area *increases* the range of the y axis (sometimes significantly)
parts:
hi

this is because the heights of the excluded data are stacked on the
unshown x value, that is, NA.

I dont know which way is better to fix, but putting below beforehand is easy:

pos_stack <- function(df, width) {
if (nrow(df) == 1) return(df)

n <- nrow(df) + 1
y <- with(df, ifelse(is.na(y), 0, y))
if(all(is.na(df$x))){
heights <- rep(0, n)
}else{
heights <- c(0, cumsum(y))
}

within(df, {
ymin <- heights[-n]
ymax <- heights[-1]
})
}

assignInNamespace("pos_stack", pos_stack, pos="package:ggplot2")
